pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q.9, a.1
pairs.question: Utrum Deus sit omnino immutabilis?
pairs.answer: Ex praemissis ostenditur Deum esse omnino immutabilem.
pairs.derivation: Article title 'Utrum Deus sit omnino immutabilis' is a genuine deliberative interrogative posed by the author. The corresponding 'Respondeo' answers it; I dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' (narration of answering) and took the operative first answering sentence to its full stop: 'Ex praemissis ostenditur Deum esse omnino immutabilem.' What follows ('Primo quidem, quia supra ostensum est...') is elaboration of the three reasons, so the answer window stops there.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q.9, a.2
pairs.question: Utrum esse immutabile sit Dei proprium?
pairs.answer: Solus Deus est omnino immutabilis: omnis autem creatura aliquo modo est mutabilis.
pairs.derivation: Article title 'Utrum esse immutabile sit Dei proprium' is a genuine deliberative interrogative posed by the author. The corresponding 'Respondeo' answers it; I dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' and took the operative first answering sentence to its full stop (keeping the internal colon, which is not a full stop): 'Solus Deus est omnino immutabilis: omnis autem creatura aliquo modo est mutabilis.' What follows ('Sciendum est enim quod...') begins the elaboration on the two senses of mutability, so the answer window stops there.
